test_title: Delhi Police Constable (Executive) 2023 - GK/CA (Held on: 29 Nov, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: gk
question: Which of the following is NOT an objective of the Fundamental Rights which are mentioned in the Indian Constitution?

options.text: Promote the ideal of political democracy
Prevent the establishment of an authoritarian and despotic rule
Establish a government of laws and not of men
Drive the citizens towards the objectives of the government

solution:
The correct answer is __**Drive the citizens towards the objectives of the government**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Fundamental Rights enshrined in the Indian Constitution aim to promote individual liberty and equality, safeguarding citizens from state excesses.
 
• They are designed to establish a framework for political democracy by guaranteeing civil liberties to all citizens.
 
• One major objective is to prevent the establishment of authoritarian or despotic rule by ensuring checks on the powers of the state.
 
• The principle of "a government of laws and not of men" is upheld by the Fundamental Rights, ensuring the rule of law in governance.
 
• However, Fundamental Rights do not aim to "drive citizens towards the objectives of the government," as their primary purpose is to protect citizens' rights and freedoms, not to enforce state-driven goals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental Rights in the Indian Constitution:**

 
 
• Enshrined in Part III of the Constitution (Articles 12-35).
 
• They are classified into six categories: Right to Equality, Right to Freedom, Right against Exploitation, Right to Freedom of Religion, Cultural and Educational Rights, and Right to Constitutional Remedies.
 
• They are enforceable by the courts, and citizens can approach the judiciary in case of violation.
 
 
 
• **Rule of Law:**
 
 
• A fundamental principle that emphasizes the supremacy of law over arbitrary powers.
 
• It ensures that all individuals, including government officials, are subject to the law.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Preventing Authoritarian Rule:**
 
 
• Fundamental Rights act as a safeguard against the concentration of power in the hands of the state or individuals.
 
• They promote democratic values by ensuring accountability, transparency, and citizen participation.
 
 
 
• **Right to Constitutional Remedies:**
 
 
• Considered the "heart and soul" of the Indian Constitution, as described by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.
 
• Allows citizens to approach the Supreme Court or High Courts to enforce Fundamental Rights through writs like Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari, and Quo Warranto.
